newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates close down on auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates close down on auction hopes.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate fell for the third session in a row on Tuesday to close down 100 basis points at 28.60 percent,
"It was stable for quite a while, then they tried to dump paper (to push rates up), but they fell back to opening levels again," said a trader.
Traders said the market market managed to shun attempts by one big dealer to raise overnight rates.
"Most trading and movement was in 28-day paper, both in government and bank issues, probably to take advantage of current rates before they fall at this evenings primary auction," a trader said.

In the term market, 28-day Cetes were traded at 29.25 percent, after not being traded at all on Monday, while 91-day and 182-day rates fell by 20 and 50 basis points, respectively, to 28.50 and 27.00 percent.
A Reuters survey of ten money market traders showed an average forecast of 29.13 percent for the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate, a fall of 21 basis points from last week's auction.
Traders said they expected rates to fall only marginally in order to maintain recent peso stability.
Banco de Mexico injected 2.017 billion pesos into the market by auctioning just one one-day credit at 30.27 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 140 basis points at 30.00 percent.
Total credit maturities for Wednesday's session were estimated at 6.789 billion pesos.
